leftEvidence.title: Zipporah and Gershom enter Moses’ story

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Moses remains with Jethro, receives Zipporah as his wife, and names their son Gershom.
points.right: At a lodging place the LORD meets “him” and seeks his death; Zipporah circumcises her son and touches the foreskin to “his feet.”

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The name remembers Moses’ life as a foreigner in a foreign land.
points.right: Zipporah speaks of a bridegroom of blood, and the threat is released after her action and words.

payload.posture: Exodus 2 establishes Zipporah as Moses’ wife and Gershom as their son before Exodus 4 calls the circumcised child only “her son.”

rightEvidence.title: Zipporah acts during a lethal encounter

payload.tension: Family continuity supports identification, but the lodging-place verses do not repeat Gershom’s name or say that only one son is present.
payload.title: The named family and the unnamed son
